elements.text: Financial infrastructure to grow your revenue
Join the millions of companies that use Stripe to accept payments online and in person, embed financial services, power custom revenue models, and build a more profitable business.

children.text: Accept cards, wallets, bank debits, and 100+ local payment methods with one integration.

elements.text: Built for developers
Every product is an API first. Test mode mirrors live mode exactly, webhooks tell your server what happened, and the CLI forwards events to localhost. Most teams take a first payment in an afternoon.

children.text: Stripe, Inc. San Francisco and Dublin.

elements.text: Payments
A complete payments platform, engineered for growth

Accept payments online, in person, and on mobile with a single integration. Checkout and the Payment Element give you a hosted or embedded payment form that adapts to the customer's country, shows the right local methods, and handles 3D Secure and SCA automatically.

Behind the form, the Payment Intents API tracks every payment from creation through authentication, capture, and refund. Radar scores every transaction for fraud using signals from the whole Stripe network, and the optimized checkout flow lifts conversion with adaptive acceptance and network tokens.
Billing
Subscriptions and invoicing for every pricing model

Model flat-rate, per-seat, tiered, and usage-based pricing without writing billing logic. Subscriptions handle proration, trials, coupons, and schedule changes; Invoices generate, send, and collect on a schedule you set.

Revenue recovery retries failed payments with a machine-learned schedule and sends reminder emails, recovering an average of 38 percent of otherwise-lost revenue. Revenue Recognition and the customer portal round it out so finance and customers can serve themselves.
Connect
Payments for platforms and marketplaces

Connect lets a platform onboard sellers or service providers, accept payments on their behalf, and route funds with a single API. Hosted onboarding collects identity and bank details and satisfies KYC requirements in 45+ countries.

Choose how money moves: direct charges on the connected account, destination charges with an application fee, or separate charges and transfers for multi-party splits. Payouts follow the schedule you set, and Express dashboards let sellers see their own balances.
Pricing
Integrated per-transaction pricing with no hidden fees. No setup fees, no monthly fees, and you only pay for what you use.

elements.text: Custom pricing

Businesses with large payment volume, unique business models, or a need for multi-product discounts can negotiate a custom package with interchange-plus pricing, volume discounts, and country-specific rates.
Customer stories
From two-person startups to companies in the Fortune 500, businesses run on Stripe.
Every story is told with the customer's permission and reviewed by their team. Want to talk to someone who has done what you are about to do? Sales can arrange a reference call.

elements.text: Questions that are not answered here are usually answered on Stack Overflow under the stripe-payments tag, or by support from the Dashboard.
Stack Overflow
Accept a payment
Build a custom payment form with the Payment Element, backed by a PaymentIntent on your server.
1. On your server, create a PaymentIntent with the amount and currency and return its client_secret to the browser. The secret is scoped to that one payment and is safe to send to the client.

children.text:
# server.py
import stripe
stripe.api_key = "sk_test_..."

intent = stripe.PaymentIntent.create(
    amount=2000, currency="usd",
    automatic_payment_methods={"enabled": True},
)
return {"clientSecret": intent.client_secret}

elements.text: 2. In the browser, load Stripe.js with your publishable key, mount the Payment Element with the client secret, and call confirmPayment when the customer submits. Stripe handles 3D Secure and redirects for methods that need them.
3. Fulfil the order from a webhook, not from the browser. Listen for payment_intent.succeeded so the order is fulfilled even if the customer closes the tab.
API reference

The Stripe API is organized around REST. It accepts form-encoded request bodies, returns JSON, and uses standard HTTP response codes and authentication. Authenticate by passing your secret key as the basic-auth user name; the current API version is 2026-08-27.

elements.text: Errors

400 invalid request, 401 bad key, 402 card declined, 404 no such object, 409 idempotency conflict, 429 rate limited, 5xx Stripe problem. Every error carries a type, a code, and a message meant for the developer, plus decline_code on card errors.
Charges

A Charge represents a single attempt to move money into your Stripe account. Newer integrations use PaymentIntents, which create Charges for you; the Charge object remains the record of what was captured, refunded, and disputed.
Endpoints
The object
Parameters
amount (integer, in the smallest currency unit) · currency (ISO code) · customer (optional) · description · metadata (up to 50 keys) · capture (default true)
Customers

A Customer object stores a payer's details, saved payment methods, and balance so you can charge them again, run subscriptions, and track history. Create one before a payment and pass its id to reuse the card.
Endpoints
The object
Parameters
email · name · phone · address · payment_method (attached on create) · invoice_settings.default_payment_method · metadata
PaymentIntents

A PaymentIntent tracks the lifecycle of one payment from creation to completion, including authentication steps and retries. Create it on your server, confirm it on the client, and read its status from webhooks.
Endpoints
The object
Parameters
Statuses: requires_payment_method → requires_confirmation → requires_action → processing → succeeded, or canceled. requires_capture appears when capture_method is manual.
Webhooks
Stripe sends an Event to your endpoint whenever something happens in your account. Use them to fulfil orders, provision subscriptions, and react to disputes.

Register an endpoint URL in the Dashboard or with the API and choose the event types you want. Each delivery is a POST with the Event JSON and a Stripe-Signature header. Verify the signature with your endpoint's signing secret before trusting the payload, and return a 2xx quickly; do the work asynchronously. Stripe retries failed deliveries with exponential backoff for up to three days.

Use the CLI in development: stripe listen --forward-to localhost:4242/webhook prints a temporary signing secret and forwards every test-mode event to your machine. Events are idempotent by id, so store the ids you have handled.
Testing
Use test mode and the test card numbers below to simulate every outcome without moving real money.
Test mode is a separate copy of your account with its own API keys (sk_test_ and pk_test_) and its own data. Any future expiry date, any three-digit CVC, and any postal code work with these numbers.

children.text:
4242 4242 4242 4242   Visa, succeeds
5555 5555 5555 4444   Mastercard, succeeds
3782 822463 10005     American Express, succeeds
4000 0025 0000 3155   Requires 3D Secure authentication
4000 0000 0000 9995   Declined: insufficient_funds
4000 0000 0000 0002   Declined: generic_decline
4000 0000 0000 0069   Declined: expired_card
4000 0000 0000 0127   Declined: incorrect_cvc

elements.text: For bank debits, the test account number 000123456789 with routing number 110000000 succeeds. To test webhooks, trigger events from the CLI with stripe trigger payment_intent.succeeded. Disputes can be simulated with the card 4000 0000 0000 0259.
API keys
Keys authenticate every request. Keep secret keys on the server, and rotate them when in doubt.

Publishable keys (pk_live_ and pk_test_) are safe to embed in a browser or mobile app; they can only create tokens and confirm payments the server set up. Secret keys (sk_live_ and sk_test_) can do anything the account can do and must never leave your server or be committed to a repository.

Restricted keys (rk_) grant a chosen subset of permissions, for example read-only access to Charges for a reporting job. Create them in the Dashboard under Developers, then API keys. Rolling a key gives you a grace period of up to 24 hours before the old key stops working.
Sign in to your account
Two-step authentication is required for every account. After your password, confirm with an authenticator app, a security key, or SMS.

elements.text: Product
Adaptive Pricing now shows local prices in 60 currencies
Sofia Lindqvist · 2026-07-15

Adaptive Pricing converts your prices into the customer's local currency at checkout and shows them a whole number that makes sense in that market. As of today it covers 60 currencies, up from 40, including every currency Stripe settles in.

In an A/B test across 3,400 businesses, showing a local price lifted conversion by 17 percent for cross-border customers. You keep receiving payouts in your settlement currency; Stripe handles the conversion and the FX rate is fixed at the time of payment.
Turn it on from the Dashboard under Payment settings. Checkout, Payment Links, and the Payment Element support it with no code change.

/blog/how-we-scaled-webhooks.title: How we rebuilt webhook delivery to handle 10 billion events a day · Stripe Blog

elements.text: Engineering
How we rebuilt webhook delivery to handle 10 billion events a day
Marcus Adeyemi · 2026-04-02

Webhook delivery looks simple: something happens, POST it to a URL. At Stripe's volume the hard parts are ordering, retries, and endpoints that are slow or down without affecting everyone else's deliveries.

The new system partitions deliveries by endpoint, so a slow endpoint only slows its own queue. Retries live in a separate tier with exponential backoff and jitter, and a circuit breaker pauses an endpoint that has failed continuously for an hour, resuming automatically when a probe succeeds.

The result: p99 delivery latency dropped from 2.4 seconds to 310 milliseconds, and the tail caused by unhealthy endpoints disappeared. If you consume webhooks, nothing changes on your side, except that events arrive sooner.
